body:
The release procedure exists only as README prose plus two throwaway scripts
that live in an agent session scratchpad and die with it: the batched
verify-then-assembleRelease Gradle run, and the wheel smoke test in a clean
venv. Every release so far has been hand-driven, which is how a release could
silently ship a stale web bundle or a mismatched APK.

Commit it as release.sh, taking the target version and doing:

1. refuse to run on a dirty tree, or off main, or if the tag already exists
2. bump every version file — server/pyproject.toml, android versionName +
   versionCode, and web/package.json (currently stuck at 0.0.0 while the README
   claims every part shares one version)
3. rebuild the web bundle
4. verify-all, then assembleRelease, in ONE gradle daemon lifetime, daemon
   stopped afterwards (the Pi is memory-tight)
5. copy the signed APK in and verify versionName/versionCode with aapt2 and the
   signature with apksigner
6. build the wheel and smoke-test it in a clean venv
7. commit and write the annotated tag

Tagging stays the last step, and stays a deliberate one.
title: release.sh — one command from version bump to tag
